title: Allocate customer receipt evidence to customer sales-invoice evidence
description: Reuse the repository's existing canonical customer-receipt evidence (FinanceReceipt) and ERP-055 customer sales-invoice evidence (CustomerSalesInvoiceEvidence) and explicitly allocate receipt amounts to recorded sales invoices. Keep the sales-order receipt-reference (ERP-053), sales-invoice-to-order (ERP-055) and receipt-to-invoice allocation dimensions separate. Do not create another receipt or invoice master, initiate or confirm real funds, infer links, post accounting, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation audits and reuses the existing canonical customer-receipt evidence and ERP-055 sales-invoice evidence, leaving one receipt master, one sales-invoice register and one explicit receipt-to-invoice allocation model.
Authorized users can allocate an eligible active customer-receipt evidence record to one or more recorded customer sales-invoice evidence records using persisted identifiers only.

The server requires authoritative Customer and currency compatibility and rejects unavailable or voided records, duplicate receipt and invoice pairs, non-positive values and allocations above either the receipt's available amount or the invoice's unallocated gross amount.
Partial allocation, one-to-many and many-to-one allocation are supported while unallocated receipt and invoice amounts remain separately visible and are never silently written off.
Different currencies are never combined or converted unless an authoritative persisted conversion already belongs to the source evidence; no current or guessed exchange rate is used.
Allocation rows preserve receipt, invoice and Customer snapshots, allocated amount, recorder and recorded time; client-supplied snapshots, balances and audit fields are not trusted.
An incorrect allocation can be voided with a bounded reason while preserving its original values and history; hard deletion, reassignment and silent amount replacement are not provided.

Sales-order receipt allocations (ERP-053), sales-invoice-to-order allocations (ERP-055) and receipt-to-invoice allocations remain distinct evidence dimensions and are not added together as if they represented separate receipts.
Missing allocations are displayed as none or unknown and are not interpreted as paid, settled, overdue, recognized revenue or posted status.
Creating, reading or voiding an allocation does not change receipt evidence, invoice status, Sales Orders, Customer balances, bank, tax, finance or settlement records.
Queries and summaries are bounded and avoid per-row access; schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit and integration tests cover partial and full allocation, multiple invoices and receipts, Customer and currency mismatch, duplicate and over-allocation rejection, void history, unavailable records, bounded summaries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Allocate one existing customer-receipt evidence record partially across two compatible recorded customer sales-invoice evidence records and verify separate remaining amounts without changing any source record or initiating funds movement.
Attempt duplicate, excessive, Customer-mismatched and currency-mismatched allocations, verify rejection, then void a valid allocation and confirm its original values and reason remain in history.

human_gate.reason: Explicit allocation of existing repository evidence only. Real receipt handling, bank access, accounting posting, production database mutation, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
